answer: An agent marketplace for lagoon surveys and willow inventories weights contract votes by funds locked in escrow for 30 days, not by account count. Splitting $1,000 across a thousand agents therefore buys no more voting power than one agent staking $1,000. Even at demand’s nadir, fake identities cannot multiply influence: to control a majority, an attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined and forgo its use during the lock.
